observations_recorded_at_seal.G2_HAS_ZERO_MARGIN_AT_THE_PILOT_GATE_FLO: The MC error table gives, at lambda=0.3 (exactly the pilot gate's fly/hold threshold): G1 5.6 sigma against a >=5 bar (+0.6 margin), G3 8.6 against >=5 (+3.6), and G2 3.0 against a >=3 bar — MARGIN EXACTLY ZERO. So if lambda_hat lands at or just above 0.3 and the flight proceeds, G2's registered verdict rests on the sigma model being exact rather than approximately right. This is not an objection and not a blocker — the pilot gate, the bars and the power table are all the arc owner's to set, and they are internally consistent. It is recorded because a gate whose power exactly equals its bar at the threshold that licenses flying is the one place where a small sigma-model error changes the verdict, and a future reader deserves to see it noted BEFORE the data rather than discovered after. >>> RESOLVED pre-GO by Amendment 1 (see amendment_1): pilot threshold 0.30 -> 0.35, bars untouched, G2 margin now +0.5.
observations_recorded_at_seal.H_2_HAS_PROPAGATED: The shortfall rule cites the H-2 clause I authored for exp142 Amendment Item 2 ('non-completion never reads as pass or fail'), and the KA gate restates it as 'unknown-is-not-a-value'. A clause written for one arc's backstop is now load-bearing in a different arc's pre-registration, applied by its author's peer rather than by me.
observations_recorded_at_seal.POOL_DISCIPLINE_IS_NOW_STRUCTURAL: The pool-re-read rule I raised at the B4 seal appears here three times — in the budget header, in the budget note, and as kill condition 4 — and has been upgraded from a caveat to a submission gate ('any stage that would overdraw the pool is not submitted'). The ask (~300 QPU-s) EXCEEDS the pool at drafting (~283 s), and staging is precisely what makes that legitimate rather than an overdraw.

what_this_entry_asserts: The text at 1359ca0, sha256 d1702ef7..., is FROZEN as of this seal and pre-dates submission.
The four registered gates with their numeric bars and frozen values, the staged budget, the degradation order, the analysis, and the kill/no-fly conditions are fixed as recorded.
The decode is frozen SS3 arithmetic with no discretion at grading time.
what_this_entry_does_NOT_assert: It does NOT assert the flight is approved — the Creator's GO was OUTSTANDING at seal time, and the ask is the largest of the H10 arc.
It does NOT assert the KA gate or the pilot gate have passed. Either can still refuse the flight, and lambda_hat < 0.15 is a hard NO-FLY.

It does NOT assert the pool can fund all four stages — it cannot at drafting (~300 QPU-s asked against ~283 s). Staging plus the per-submission pool re-read is what makes the ask legitimate; a stage that would overdraw is simply not submitted.
It does NOT assert anything about outcomes, nor that the registered gates are the RIGHT gates — only that they were fixed before the data existed.
